description: Nominalisierung (nominalization) is the process of converting verbs, adjectives, and other word classes into nouns in German. This includes: nominalized infinitives (das Lesen), -ung nouns (die Lösung), -heit/-keit nouns (die Freiheit/die MögLichkeit), -tion/-sion nouns (die Organisation), and adjective nominalizations (das Neue, der Bekannte). Key skills: choosing the correct article/gender, forming compound nouns, using nominalizations in formal written register, and applying the correct case (Genitiv/Dativ) after prepositions.
tips: Nominalized infinitive: das + Verb stem + -en → das Lesen, das Schreiben, das Analysieren. Always neuter (das), always singular.
-ung suffix: verb → feminine noun → die Lösung (from lösen), die Einstellung (from einstellen), die Verlängerung (from verlängern). Strongly preferred in formal/business German.
-heit suffix: adjective → feminine noun → die Freiheit (frei), die Gesundheit (gesund), die Möglichkeit (möglich). Used for abstract concepts.
-keit suffix: adjective → feminine noun → die Möglichkeit (möglich), die Einsamkeit (einsam). Similar to -heit, often used with adjectives ending in -lich, -ig, -sam.
Genitiv after prepositions: 'trotz' (Genitiv) → trotz der Niederlage; 'wegen' (Genitiv) → wegen der Verzögerung; 'statt' (Genitiv) → statt des Streitens.
Preposition + nominalized infinitive phrase: statt des Aufgebens (Genitiv preposition + nominalized infinitive in Genitiv). Compare: statt aufzugeben (infinitive clause — also correct).
Two coordinated nominalizations: das Erkennen und Lösen (both nominative, shared 'das'). When dependent on Genitiv preposition: des Erkennens und Lösens.
Adjective before nominalized infinitive: das rasche Reagieren — adjective takes weak declension after 'das' → -e ending.
Genitiv complement after nouns: die Notwendigkeit der Modernisierung, die Bedeutung des nachhaltigen Wirtschaftens. Adjective takes Genitiv weak ending -en.
Im Hinblick auf + Akkusativ: das vermehrte Auftreten (Akkusativ neuter -e weak ending) + Genitiv dependent noun: resistenter Keime.

questions.questionText: Das ____ der Aufgabe hat länger gedauert als erwartet.
questions.explanation: The nominalized infinitive 'das Lösen' (the solving) is a neuter noun formed directly from the verb 'lösen'. It refers to the process/act of solving. 'Lösung' means the result/solution, not the act — which changes the meaning here.

questions.questionText: Statt ____ könnte man auch einen Kompromiss finden.
questions.explanation: 'Statt' (instead of) is a preposition that governs the Genitiv case. The nominalized infinitive 'das Streiten' → Genitiv: 'des Streitens'. 'zu streiten' is an infinitive clause, not a nominalization, and cannot follow 'statt' directly.

questions.questionText: Die ____ der neuen Mitarbeiter findet nächste Woche statt.
questions.explanation: 'Die Einstellung' is the standard nominalization of 'einstellen' using the suffix '-ung' (feminine). In formal/business German, '-ung' nominalizations are preferred over infinitive nominalizations. Here it refers to the hiring/onboarding event.

questions.questionText: Das ____ der Kinder im Park macht Freude.
questions.explanation: The nominalized infinitive 'das Lachen' (the laughing/laughter) refers to the general act or sound of laughing. 'Gelächter' is also a valid noun but means loud/burst of laughter and changes the nuance. 'Gelache' (with Ge- prefix) can carry a negative connotation.

questions.questionText: Trotz ____ blieb das Team motiviert.
questions.explanation: 'Trotz' (despite) governs the Genitiv case. 'Die Niederlage' (the defeat) → Genitiv singular: 'der Niederlage'. 'dem Verlieren' uses Dativ, which is incorrect after 'trotz' in standard written German.

questions.questionText: Das ____ von Daten ist in vielen Berufen unverzichtbar.
questions.explanation: The nominalized infinitive 'das Analysieren' (the analyzing) describes the ongoing process. 'Analysierung' is not a standard German word. 'Analyse' is a valid noun but means the analysis (result), not the act of analyzing.

questions.questionText: Die ____ des Vertrags wurde von beiden Seiten unterzeichnet.
questions.explanation: 'Die Verlängerung' (the extension/renewal) is the standard '-ung' nominalization of 'verlängern'. In formal written German, '-ung' nominalizations are strongly preferred in bureaucratic and legal contexts. '-nis' and '-ei' are not used with this verb.

questions.questionText: Wegen ____ des Projekts mussten alle Pläne verschoben werden.
questions.explanation: 'Wegen' (because of) governs Genitiv. 'Die Verzögerung' → Genitiv: 'der Verzögerung'. The phrase 'wegen des Projekts' is already in Genitiv; the nominalization must also be in Genitiv. 'dem Verzögern' uses Dativ — incorrect after 'wegen' in written German.

questions.questionText: Das ____ der Aufgaben an die Teammitglieder ist eine wichtige Führungskompetenz.
questions.explanation: 'Die Delegation' is the preferred nominalization in the management/business register for 'delegieren'. While 'das Delegieren' is grammatically correct, 'Delegation' is the established noun used in formal contexts. 'Delegierung' is non-standard and rarely used.

questions.questionText: Durch ____ konnte das Unternehmen seine Kosten erheblich senken.
questions.explanation: 'Durch' (through/by) requires a noun phrase. 'Das Optimieren der Prozesse' is a nominalized infinitive phrase acting as the object of 'durch'. This structure (Präposition + nominalized infinitive + Genitiv object) is a key B2 written-register pattern.

questions.questionText: Anstatt ____ schlug er eine alternative Lösung vor.
questions.explanation: 'Anstatt' (instead of) is a Genitiv preposition. The nominalized infinitive 'das Aufgeben' → Genitiv: 'des Aufgebens'. Note: 'anstatt aufzugeben' (with infinitive clause) is also correct German, but the question asks for the nominalization form.

questions.questionText: Das ____ und ____ von Konflikten gehört zu den wichtigsten Managementfähigkeiten.
questions.explanation: When two nominalized infinitives are coordinated as subject with 'und', they both take the nominative form: 'das Erkennen und Lösen'. Only the first 'das' is needed. Genitiv forms ('Erkennens/Lösens') would be needed after a Genitiv preposition, not as subject.

questions.questionText: Im Bericht wird auf die Notwendigkeit ____ der Infrastruktur hingewiesen.
questions.explanation: After 'die Notwendigkeit' (the necessity), a Genitiv complement is required. 'Die Modernisierung' (modernization) → Genitiv: 'der Modernisierung'. The '-ung' form is standard in formal/official language. 'des Modernisierens' is grammatically possible but marked as colloquial.

questions.questionText: Das rasche ____ auf Krisen ist entscheidend für den Erfolg von Einsatzkräften.
questions.explanation: 'Das rasche Reagieren' (the rapid reacting) uses a nominalized infinitive modified by an adjective ('rasche'). The adjective takes weak declension after 'das' → 'rasch-e'. 'Reaktion' is also a valid noun but 'rasche Reaktion' would need 'die', not 'das', changing the article.

questions.questionText: Trotz aller Bemühungen scheiterte ____ eines gemeinsamen Kompromisses.
questions.explanation: 'Scheiterte' (failed) requires a nominative subject. 'Das Finden eines gemeinsamen Kompromisses' acts as the subject of the sentence. The nominalized infinitive 'das Finden' is nominative. 'des Findens' is Genitiv and cannot be the subject.

questions.questionText: Der Vorstand betonte die Bedeutung ____ in allen Bereichen des Unternehmens.
questions.explanation: 'Die Bedeutung' (the significance) takes a Genitiv complement. Nominalized infinitive in Genitiv: 'des + adjective (Genitiv weak: -en) + Verb-en + -s' → 'des nachhaltigen Wirtschaftens'. The adjective 'nachhaltig' takes the Genitiv weak ending '-en' after the definite article 'des'.

questions.questionText: Durch ____ wurden erhebliche Fortschritte in der Forschung erzielt.
questions.explanation: After 'durch' (Akkusativ), the nominalized infinitive takes 'das' + adjective weak ending (-e in Akkusativ neuter): 'das konsequente Vorantreiben'. The dependent noun 'Zusammenarbeit' becomes Genitiv: 'interdisziplinärer Zusammenarbeit'. 'Vorantreibung' is not a standard German word.

questions.questionText: Im Hinblick auf ____ wurden neue Richtlinien erlassen.
questions.explanation: 'Im Hinblick auf' (with regard to) governs Akkusativ. Nominalized infinitive: 'das + adjective (Akk. neuter weak: -e) + Infinitiv' → 'das vermehrte Auftreten'. Dependent noun 'Keime' → Genitiv: 'resistenter Keime'. 'des Auftretens' would be Genitiv, not Akkusativ.

questions.questionText: Die Herausforderung besteht im ____ unterschiedlicher Interessen ohne Qualitätsverlust.
questions.explanation: 'Im' = 'in + dem' (Dativ). Nominalized infinitive in Dativ: 'im + Infinitiv (no article change for neuter Dativ in this fixed 'im + Nominalisierung' construction)' → 'im Ausbalancieren'. This is a high-frequency B2 formal pattern: 'bestehen in + Dativ nominalized infinitive'. '-ierung' and '-heit' suffixes are non-standard here.

questions.questionText: Obwohl man sich ____ des Problems bewusst war, fehlte es an konkreten Maßnahmen.
questions.explanation: 'Sich bewusst sein' (to be aware of) takes a Genitiv object. The nominalization 'die Komplexität' (complexity) — formed from the adjective 'komplex' with the suffix '-ität' (a productive B2+ nominalization pattern) — becomes Genitiv: 'der Komplexität'. The '-ität' suffix always produces feminine nouns.
